selections.comment: Karl Burke, James Doyle and Wathnan Racing teamed up to land this race 12 months ago with Leovanni and they could repeat the dose courtesy of ZELAINA. The daughter of Mehmas was an impressive winner on her debut at Nottingham, the same race in which Leovanni made a successful racecourse bow, and this 650,000-pound Breeze-Up purchase could be yet another exciting youngster for a stable that have been leading the way with their juveniles this term. Michael Bell was glowing in his review of Spicy Marg, who made a winning debut at Newmarket, and she is well worth considering, along with the likes of C&D winner Society Kiss and Marygate victor Secret Hideaway.

selections.comment: Having enjoyed success on eight previous occasions, Aidan O'Brien's record in this race is impeccable and the Ballydoyle trainer again has live contenders in the shape of Shackleton and Scandinavia, who are potential improvers over this distance. John & Thady Gosden's yard also has a strong association with this event and their representative, Devil's Advocate, is another must for any shortlist given his dam was a Group 3 winner over 1m6f. However, CARMERS had this race nominated immediately after his facile success in the Yeats Stakes over 1m5f at Navan and, with the ground likely to be ideal, this unbeaten son of Wootton Bassett looks the most attractive proposition. French raider Asmarani can also go well if he handles the forecast going.

Karl Burke's filly isn't taken lightly, but CINDERELLA'S DREAM is the more solid proposition. One Look lost little in defeat against multiple Group 1 winner Porta Fortuna at the Curragh in May and another good account is forecast, while the addition of cheekpieces may help Running Lion.

selections.comment: A high-class renewal is likely to be headed by Los Angeles, who recorded his third Group 1 success when defeating ANMAAT (second) in the Tattersalls Gold Cup at the Curragh last month. Typically, Aidan O'Brien is no stranger to success in this race but, although respected, Owen Burrows' talented seven-year-old can turn the tables. The son of Awtaad was seemingly going best of all two furlongs from home that day and if stepping forward from that seasonal return, he could add further success to an already stellar CV. Middleton winner See The Fire was supplemented for 70,000 pounds and is interesting receiving the fillies' allowance, while Prix Ganay runner-up Map Of Stars and the progressive Ombudsman add further spice to the race.

selections.comment: My Cloud is two from two since competing in handicaps, most recently beating a subsequent winner by a head at Newbury, and it's easy to see why he will have his supporters. The Liffey wasn't disgraced when fourth in a Listed contest at Naas last month and that effort is likely to have put him spot on for this under Ryan Moore, but a chance can be taken on HI ROYAL. Kevin Ryan's five-year-old has plenty of class as the runner-up of the 2023 edition of the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket and he bounced back to form when second at Thirsk last month. This race could be perfectly run to suit and he looks the way to go.

selections.comment: Having finished a fine second in a Listed event over 7f at Musselburgh 11 days ago, Arolla must enter the reckoning on her handicap bow. Harry Charlton's filly looks fairly treated racing off an official rating of 100 and reverting to 1m shouldn't prevent another bold showing. selections.comment: A wide-open contest to end proceedings on another enthralling day of racing, and only a tentative vote can go to HAVANA HURRICANE. A striking winner on his debut at Goodwood before going on to finish an excellent second in the Woodcote at Epsom, despite not appearing to be in love with the track, he brings a useful level of form to the table and might offer some value against the likes of Rogue Legend and Beverley Two Year Old Trophy winner Old Is Gold, who runs in the colours of Wathnan Racing for the first time. US raider Tough Critic should not be overlooked, while similar comments apply to the David O'Meara-trained Rogue Supremacy.

selections.comment: RORY ROCKET is the logical selection based on his two promising starts as a juvenile last autumn. The son of Aclaim filled the runner-up spot in both of those races, showing versatility in ground preference by adeptly switching from good to firm going to heavy. As his dam is a half-sister to a winner on all-weather, a synthetic track should also be within his compass. With first-time blinkers tried, Saguaro Blossom is an obvious threat, while Apple Of My Eye is the pick of the rest.

Of those that contested the Marygate it is Love Olivia who could reverse form with her re-opposing rivals and fare best. She went too fast when placed that day but showed she had plenty of speed so is dangerous if getting a break on the field on quick ground here.

He could complete the places ahead of Shackleton who looks the pick of the pair from last year's winning yard but does appear to have had his limitations exposed.

selections.comment: A good renewal where plenty re-oppose from the Champion Stakes over C&D. Anmaat was successful that day under a well timed ride and he proved he retained his ability when runner up to Los Angeles in the Tattersalls Gold Cup on his return. He arguably travelled best that day before the Irish Derby winner's fitness edge told late and that form could be reversed here. However the pair could both be vulnerable to SEE THE FIRE who finished midfield here in the autumn showpieces but met plenty of trouble that day and she's taken her form to a new level this year with an emphatic 12l romp in the Middleton. She is yet to prove quite as effective away from York but looks worth another chance in favourable fast conditions. The progressive lightly raced pair Map Of Stars and Ombudsman are also respected. The former's runner up effort in the Prix Ganay has been franked in the Prix D'Ispahan but he has work to do to reverse form with the latter from last year's Prix du Prince d'Orange.

My Cloud did well to catch one who got first run last time to complete a hat trick and that rival has franked the form so he should hold every chance off this revised mark. THE LIFFEY appeals more though having caught the eye on his reappearance meeting trouble in the Owenstown Stud Stakes. Both that run and his debut effort have been franked multiple times at Group level so he could prove leniently treated off an opening mark of 98. The step back up in distance, the booking of Moore and the addition of cheekpieces all signal that further improvement is likely. Hi Royal returned to form when runner up in the Thirsk Hunt Cup last time and is entitled to come on for that run. He's been raised 2lb to a mark of 104 but in 2023 was recording ratings as high as 117 when placing in the Guineas and it may just be that he's back close to his peak. If that's the case he could prove good each way value along with Silawi who justified strong support when proving his ability on fast ground last time. He remains well treated on his French Group form and if coping with the drop in trip should remain competitive. The consistent Qirat is also respected given his good record here though he holds no secrets from the handicapper.

selections.comment: Richard Fahey has a 17% win strike rate at Hamilton over the last 5 years, and his filly AWAAFI is bred to be an absolute speedball. She is related to Kylian, who is a multiple winner over 5 furlongs and is currently rated 103; therefore, the pedigree would suggest she could be very smart and pretty quick. This isn't the strongest novice race in the world, so connections looked to have found the perfect starting point for her. Baggot Street has the benefit of the experience under his belt, and he bumped into a smart-looking type last time out. In slightly calmer waters now, he will run well again here. Aspiral hails from a top yard, and although she wasn't an expensive purchase, she will no doubt be tuned and ready to run well here.

selections.comment: CANON'S HOUSE has kickstarted this season in brilliant form, and he looks to be a completely different proposition this season. He is 17 lb higher in the weights compared to the first victory at Carlisle in May, but given the fact he has won both contests by a combined 9 and a half lengths, he probably deserves to get the hike in the weights he has gotten. Given the fact he made all and won comfortably last time out, there could still be even more to come from this lad who is in very good form at present. Bona Fortuna was in good form last season when landing two contests in a row after changing yards to Mick Appleby's; he ran well at York in a big field last time out, and now having his 2nd run after a wind operation, he could go well but might have to settle for 2nd behind an in-form rival. Woohoo has won her last 3 races, and although this would take a career best to win, she is clearly in the right form to fill the placings here.

selections.comment: It was a bit of a messy contest that IRIS DANCER won at Hamilton last time out, as he drifted left and was sort of running all over the place in the final stages but still managed to get his head in front with Havana Rum in 2nd. The latter escapes a rise in the weights for this race, but Iris Dancer was always doing enough to win in the closing stages, and although he has a 4 lb higher mark to deal with here, he is still 7 lb lower than his peak mark from last season. There is still more to come from the Tristan Davidson runner here. Havana Rum was a good 2nd last time out, and he might serve it up to his rival here again, but will ultimately finish 2nd to him once again. Belsito has been running well lately, and he could be the one to fill the places here.

Sands Of Indi comes from a top yard and was a nice enough winner last time out; she runs off the same mark here as it was only 2 days ago, and Jack Nicholls takes his very valuable apprentice allowance off her back here; she can run well and place here. Blufferonthebus was a decent 2nd last time out, and she might be able to build on that and fill the placings here.

Obito is yet to win but has placed on two separate occasions; he can go well here and place once again before progressing onwards.

And Paper Doll put in a very good performance on stable debut, coming 3rd at Catterick; he could improve but might have to just settle with filling the places here.

The most solid is WRITTENINTHESTARS who managed a fair third last time when kicking off this campaign a couple of weeks back. That was on handicap debut and there's a chance a he can find a bit more but may not need it in this company. Ejuna is interersting in first time blinkers tried at 5f for the first time. Prior to that blip Charlie Wallis's gelding was consistently competitive in handicap company and won last time dropped to Classified Stakes level in January. He should go close. Poet looks next best but needs to leave a couple of miserable efforts on turf well behind him returned to the all-weather. He's mostly campaigned on Tapeta but won on Polytrack at Kempton (6f) early in his career and was beaten about two lengths here over 6f on season debut this year on his only other try on it. He can put up a stern challenge. Blackbrook is interesting dropped back to 6f for the first time having struggled over 1m the last twice. Before that he managed a good forth of 12 at Kempton in a decent novice. That probably flatters him somewhat but a big step forward on handicap form so far could be in the offing

Isle Of Sark arrives in good shape after a promising narrow margin defeat last time. A repeat of that would leave him with some ground to make up but he rated much higher in a busy season last term and can take another step forward to attaining those levels again. He might be able to dictate matters and looks the main danger. Simiyann can't be discounted if bouncing back returned to this grade

He won't go down easily. Glint Of Light can play a role but likely just a bit part

selections.comment: MR TRICK looks the safest choice in a desparately moderate affair. He has to bounce back after a poor effort last time but went close two weeks earlier under the same conditions (both class 6 handicaps at Leicester over 10f on good to firm ground) and a replication of that will likely be enough to take the top prize. Offiah's Boy has more misses than hits but if giving best is entitled to figure and was a head in front of the selection when second at Leicester in May and is a couple of pounds better off. However, he's much less reliable and the selection had an awkward start that day and can do a bit better. Mond has form claims but is impossible to get a handle on having raced over 1m4f last time but 6f the time before and on balance is best watched until finding his optimum conditions so Regal Glory may prove the biggest threat to the principals given he's at least got competitive on a few occasions in the last six months or so
